scores.evidence: In practice the switchover may need a short write freeze (seconds to a few minutes).
scores.rationale: Technical claims about CDC (Always On, DMS, Debezium), DNS TTL, interface-engine queuing and HIPAA retention are accurate, and the plan honestly states the real limit of 'zero downtime'.

scores.evidence: "Zero downtime" means users never see an outage.
scores.rationale: Directly solves the stated problem, resolves the zero-downtime ambiguity sensibly, states assumptions, and is clearly buildable with modernization explicitly deferred.

scores.evidence: Only one system accepts bookings at any moment.
scores.rationale: The single-write-authority principle, interface-engine as the HL7 switch, and reverse replication for rollback are applied consistently across every phase with no contradictions.

scores.evidence: run the full switchover **at least twice** in a pre-production copy, including the rollback. Time each step.
scores.rationale: Validation targets the specific risks (shadow reads, peak replay, failover drills, continuous data checks, rehearsed rollback) before commitment and continues post-cutover with dashboards and daily reconciliation.

scores.evidence: It assumes a US hospital (HIPAA), a scheduling app backed by a relational database, and connections to the EHR
scores.rationale: Assumptions are stated up front, the timeline is labeled rough, the approach table shows how answers would change the design, and clarifying questions identify sensitivities.

scores.evidence: Double-booking or lost appointments | One system takes bookings at a time, continuous data checks, queued messages
scores.rationale: The major domain failures (double-booking, broken interfaces, latency, ransomware, data mismatch) have concrete detection and recovery, but duplicate/out-of-order HL7 messages on queue replay are not addressed.

scores.evidence: Dashboards: response time, error rates, HL7 queue depth and acknowledgment failures, reminder delivery rates, booking volume against the usual baseline
scores.rationale: Domain-meaningful health signals, command center, hypercare, IaC, rollback path, runbook updates and clear clinical ownership make this operable by a realistic hospital IT team.

scores.evidence: Later improvements: cost tuning, managed services, a FHIR scheduling API, autoscaling.
scores.rationale: Costs are essentially ignored: no cost drivers (dual-running infrastructure, Direct Connect, licensing, engineering effort), no estimates or controls beyond a passing 'cost tuning' mention.

scores.evidence: Have a way back at every step... Keep the on-prem system **warm for 30–60 days** as a rollback option
scores.rationale: The one-way cutover decision gets the most scrutiny with reverse replication and rehearsed rollback, modernization is deferred to avoid compounding risk, and reversible choices are made quickly.

scores.evidence: Don't change the platform and the app at the same time.
scores.rationale: Recommends the simplest workable approach (lift and shift with CDC), explicitly rejects simultaneous re-architecting, and every component is justified by the no-downtime and safety needs.

scores.evidence: Put the old system in **read-only/maintenance mode**... Wait until the copy has fully caught up, then run the final data check.
scores.rationale: Dependency-ordered phases with week ranges, a numbered switchover runbook, explicit rollback triggers, and checkable intermediate results let a team start immediately; remaining tool choices depend only on acknowledged unknowns.

checklist.evidence: A **Business Associate Agreement (BAA)** with the cloud provider is required before any patient data moves.
HL7 v2 feeds with the EHR... Patient portal... Reminder systems... Billing... Reports and data warehouse feeds... check-in kiosks
row counts, checksums per table, and business-level checks (appointments per provider per day, open slots, waitlists)
Only one system accepts bookings at any moment... aim for under 5 minutes of write freeze
run the full switchover **at least twice** in a pre-production copy, including the rollback
a dedicated private link (Direct Connect, ExpressRoute) with a VPN backup. Test latency from clinic workstations
spread across multiple availability zones... Backups: automated, immutable, and restore-tested... print the next 72 hours of schedules as a backup
connect to existing AD and single sign-on. Least-privilege access, multi-factor authentication for admins
replay peak-hour load, plus a margin... send copies of real read traffic (or replay recorded traffic) to the cloud and compare responses
target a low-volume window, e.g., Sunday early morning... Change freeze... Brief staff... IT staff on site at large clinics
Get written vendor approval for cloud hosting before Phase 2... Securely wipe old storage according to NIST 800-88

traps.evidence: Continuous copying (CDC) from on-prem to cloud... run the full switchover at least twice in a pre-production copy, including the rollback
Old and new systems must never both take writes. Copy data one way, then switch over once.
Test every connection from start to finish in the cloud test environment with realistic (de-identified) messages.
If you have an interface engine (Rhapsody, Cloverleaf, Mirth, Corepoint), use it to send messages to old or new.
Modernize after the move is stable. Don't change the platform and the app at the same time.

note: An exemplary, trap-free migration plan with correct single-write-authority cutover, rehearsed rollback, and full interface coverage; its only material weaknesses are near-total silence on cost, missing break-glass access, and unaddressed duplicate-message handling on queue replay.
